title: Structural Room Feature Implementation Plan

notes: Manifest now reflects the structural room implementation as actively in progress.
Completion checks cover shell thickness, openings, placement readiness, feature slicing, selection alignment, and canonical face contract alignment.

featureSlice.name: rooms/structural
constraints: Geometry, types, hooks, and components must remain separated
Room rendering must be derived from room structure data rather than ad hoc mesh logic
Future procedural object placement must be supported through explicit metadata
Selection must anchor to the visible room face, not a brittle hardcoded offset
Canonical room face contract treats top as ceiling and bottom as floor

axiomatic: Rooms are architectural structures with physical thickness, not symbolic boxes
Openings must be structural cutouts in the room shell
Room-local geometry and metadata must be the source of truth for future procedural interior placement
The room shell, not the renderer, is authoritative for wall, floor, ceiling, and opening semantics
axiological: Prioritize realism, clarity, extensibility, and GPU-friendly performance
Preserve the existing room silhouette while upgrading it to true architectural depth
Avoid overfitting to current assets so the system can scale to future room types
Prefer deterministic, validated geometry over visually fragile hacks
teleological: Evolve room rendering into a reusable structural system for thick walls, floors, ceilings, windows, doors, and cutaways
Create a stable foundation for future procedural furniture and interior object placement
Deliver visually credible rooms without introducing monolithic rendering code
Enable room structure to support future layout intelligence, adjacency rules, and procedural decoration

structuralPrinciples: Room structure is the canonical source of truth
Renderable geometry is always derived from structural data
Placement metadata must be independent of mesh tessellation
Cutaway and debug states must never mutate the authoritative room model
Every generated structure must be deterministic from identical inputs
Structural face semantics must map top to ceiling and bottom to floor
scope: Support parametric openings for windows and doors
Create room-local anchors and exclusion zones for future procedural placement
Keep rendering, structure, and validation logic feature-sliced
Preserve compatibility with the current simulation and selection systems
Support cutaway-friendly room visibility without sacrificing shell realism
Maintain compatibility migration from the current room component to the structural room system
objectives: Replace thin room representations with thick architectural shells
Support clean cutaways for visibility into room interiors
Allow windows and doors to be modeled as true shell openings
Provide metadata for future object placement and room decoration
Keep the implementation decomposed into small feature-sliced modules
Ensure the selection indicator aligns to the room's visible front face

workstreams.name: Room structure model
goals: Represent rooms as physical shells with wall, floor, and ceiling thickness
Store structure data separately from rendering details
Keep the room definition deterministic and serializable
Model visible face references and placement bands as part of the room contract

phases.name: Room structural schema
tasks: Define room shell thickness fields
Define opening definitions with wall association and offsets
Define anchor points for walls, floor, ceiling, and openings
Define exclusion zones for future furniture placement
Define face references for visible front, back, and side selection alignment

phases.name: Geometry generation contract
tasks: Derive all renderable room geometry from the room structure model
Ensure geometry generation is repeatable from identical inputs
Keep shell, opening, and frame generation isolated into reusable helpers
Separate selection-facing geometry references from render-only meshes

workstreams.name: Room opening system
goals: Support windows, doors, and door openings as structural cutouts
Maintain a believable wall reveal depth around openings
Keep openings valid across thick shell and cutaway configurations

phases.name: Parametric opening definitions
tasks: Define opening width, height, wall target, and offset
Support sill, lintel, jamb, and threshold metadata
Validate openings against wall boundaries and thickness
Classify openings by semantic role such as transparent, pass-through, or cutaway-only

phases.name: Cutout and reveal generation
tasks: Subtract openings from shell geometry cleanly
Generate frame/reveal geometry around openings
Prevent sliver geometry, cracks, and z-fighting
Ensure reveal depth remains visually credible at oblique camera angles

workstreams.name: Room placement foundation
goals: Prepare the system for future procedural interior object placement
Keep placement rules independent from rendered mesh details
Expose stable spatial zones for safe object generation
Represent placement as semantic bands rather than raw mesh coordinates

phases.name: Anchor generation
tasks: Derive stable room-local anchors for wall, floor, and ceiling placement
Derive no-placement zones around openings and shell thickness
Expose placement metadata in a reusable, serializable format
Include room-local placement bands for wall decor, floor furniture, and ceiling fixtures

phases.name: Future procedural hooks
tasks: Provide hook points for room furniture and decor generation
Keep placement logic compatible with future procedural systems
Avoid coupling object placement to geometry implementation details
Allow semantic reservation of circulation paths and opening-adjacent clearances

workstreams.name: Room cutaway and visibility
goals: Support cutaway-friendly visibility for interior inspection
Keep selection and debug visibility separate from physical room data
Ensure the room remains visually readable as a structured interior volume

phases.name: Visibility policy
tasks: Define when cutaway visibility applies
Keep structural cutaway state non-destructive
Separate selection visibility from debug visibility

phases.name: Selection alignment
tasks: Anchor the selection indicator to the room's visible front face
Avoid hardcoded front-face offsets
Keep selection stable under thickness, openings, and rotation

qualityGuards: All room structure should be derived from room-local source data
Separate structure, rendering, selection, and placement concerns
Preserve temporal stability and avoid geometry-driven flicker or drift
Keep opening generation deterministic and repeatable
Prefer reusable helpers and feature-sliced modules over inline geometry logic
Maintain a single authoritative room model and derive all other representations from it

strategy: Log room shell dimensions, opening bounds, and generated anchors during development
Add debug overlays for shell thickness, opening cutouts, and exclusion zones
Validate room geometry after generation for seams, zero-area fragments, and alignment errors
Verify selection indicator anchoring against the room's visible front face
Isolate structure, opening, and placement failures with feature flags
Capture deterministic room-structure snapshots for regression comparison
Track selection face references separately from mesh geometry during debug runs

completionChecks.name: Structural fidelity
criteria: Rooms render with believable thick walls, floor, and ceiling
The room silhouette remains readable from the current camera perspective
Structural thickness is visually apparent without collapsing into a white cube
Wall, floor, and ceiling thickness remain consistent with the structural model
The room can be regenerated from the same input without altering topology

completionChecks.name: Opening correctness
criteria: Windows and doors are true openings in the shell
Openings preserve reveal depth and structural readability
No visible cracks, slivers, or z-fighting appear around openings
Opening bounds remain fully contained within their target wall faces
Opening semantics remain consistent for doors, windows, and future cutaway apertures

completionChecks.name: Placement readiness
criteria: Room-local anchors are available for future procedural interior objects
Exclusion zones prevent invalid placement near openings and shell edges
Placement metadata is deterministic and separate from render-only geometry
Placement bands support floor, wall, and ceiling use cases
Placement rules can be evaluated independently of the rendered mesh

completionChecks.name: Feature-sliced integrity
criteria: Room logic is split across dedicated structural feature files
No new monolithic room implementation file is introduced
Geometry, types, and components remain separated by responsibility
Hooks or adapters orchestrate derived state instead of embedding generation inline
Shared helpers remain reusable and do not depend on presentation-layer state

completionChecks.name: Visibility and selection alignment
criteria: Selection anchors to the room's visible front face rather than a fixed offset
Cutaway visibility does not alter the authoritative room model
Selection remains stable across room rotation and thickness changes
Debug overlays do not mutate structure or placement data

definitionOfDone: Rooms are rendered as thick structural shells
Openings are generated as true architectural cutouts
Selection aligns to the visible room face
Placement metadata exists for future procedural interior objects
The implementation remains feature-sliced and avoids monolithic files
Debugging and completion checks confirm structural correctness and visual stability
Room structure remains the canonical source of truth for all derived visuals and metadata
